sentences.text: The known fossil consists of a nearly complete, articulated skeleton that lacks a skull but preserves soft tissue remains including feathers.
Parahongshanornis was a small bird with a femur measuring twenty-four millimetres in length.
The furcula of Parahongshanornis is U-shaped, and the coracoid is elongated with a broad end that touches the sternum.
Parahongshanornis is considered the youngest known member of the family Hongshanornithidae.
The genus Parahongshanornis and its type species P. chaoyangensis were named by Li Li, Wang Jingqi, and Hou Shilin in 2011.
The holotype specimen PMOL-AB00161 was found near Yuanjiawa, Chaoyang, in the Jiufotang Formation of the Jehol Biota, dating to about 120 million years ago.
Parahongshanornis was assigned to the family Hongshanornithidae based on comparative anatomy rather than cladistic analysis.
Parahongshanornis lived during the Aptian stage of the lower Cretaceous in what is now Liaoning Province, north-eastern China.
The time range for Parahongshanornis is estimated from 121.4 to 113.2 million years ago.
